new_value: Donald Richardson was 21 when he started the band at Andrew J. Bell Junior High in Tremé in the 1963-64 school year, with 28 drummers and 15 trumpet players. He built the Marching Crusaders into a parade band that in 1985 became the first junior high band to march in Rex on Mardi Gras Day. His students included Kirk and Charles Joseph, who joined the Dirty Dozen Brass Band, several later brass band leaders and school band directors, and Derrick Tabb of the Rebirth Brass Band, who modeled his Roots of Music program on Bell. Richardson died in 1995. The school never reopened after Hurricane Katrina in 2005; since 2018 its buildings have housed artists as the Bell Artspace Campus.

After about ten moves between borrowed and leased rooms, the organization bought the former St. Gabriel Catholic Church property on Piety Drive in June 2025.
